safety_evidence.plant_part_used: root (huang qin; kampo and TCM formulas)

drug_interactions.effect: isolated baicalin lowered rosuvastatin AUC ~9-47 %, haplotype-dependent

adverse_event_history.statement: All reports found involve mixtures, with the test article named: (1) flavocoxid (Limbrel), baicalin + catechins from S. baicalensis and Acacia catechu - four DILIN liver-injury cases, all recovered; (2) Move Free Advanced (Chinese skullcap with glucosamine/chondroitin) - liver injury, one case with pneumonitis; (3) Sho-saiko-to, a seven-herb kampo formula including S. baicalensis root - hepatocellular injury (LiverTox score B) and interstitial pneumonitis described as uncommon (a cited review counted 19 cases), with S. baicalensis the suspected component.
adverse_event_history.md: All reports found involve mixtures, with the [test article](#term:test-article) named: (1) flavocoxid (Limbrel), baicalin + catechins from S. baicalensis and Acacia catechu - four DILIN liver-injury cases, all [recovered](#term:extraction-yield); (2) Move Free Advanced (Chinese skullcap with glucosamine/chondroitin) - [liver injury](#term:hepatotoxicity), one case with pneumonitis; (3) [Sho-saiko-to](#term:sho-saiko-to), a seven-herb kampo formula including S. baicalensis root - hepatocellular injury ([LiverTox](#term:livertox) score B) and interstitial pneumonitis described as uncommon (a cited review counted 19 cases), with S. baicalensis the suspected component.

constituents_of_concern.concern: OATP1B1-mediated interaction; hepatotoxicity reported with the baicalin + catechin product flavocoxid
constituents_of_concern.md: [OATP1B1-mediated](#term:oatp) [interaction](#term:drug-interaction); hepatotoxicity reported with the baicalin + catechin product flavocoxid

evidence.claim: A multi-herb kampo formula containing S. baicalensis root is associated with liver injury and interstitial pneumonitis.
evidence.test_article_detail: Sho-saiko-to (7 herbs incl. Scutellaria baicalensis root)
evidence.outcome_summary: Case reports/series summarised by LiverTox; causal component unknown, S. baicalensis suspected.

evidence.claim: A baicalin-containing medical food caused clinically significant liver injury.
evidence.test_article_detail: flavocoxid (baicalin + catechins; S. baicalensis + Acacia catechu)
evidence.outcome_summary: Four cases, onset 1-3 months, recovery within 12 weeks of stopping.
